previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a flare characterized by chest pain, shortness of breath, epigastric pain, and total body pain. She self-administered an EpiPen prior to arrival due to concern for anaphylaxis but presented without hypotension or wheezing. She was treated with her established IV regimen of hydromorphone, lorazepam, and diphenhydramine as per her outpatient protocol. Imaging showed bibasilar atelectasis and no acute cardiopulmonary findings. Labs revealed mild leukocytopenia, likely chronic. Her symptoms improved gradually, and she was transitioned to oral medications. No changes were made to her chronic regimen. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her primary care provider and allergist.
problems: Other specified disorders involving the immune mechanism
Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx, unspecified
